summary: Canadian Coast Guard light on the Saint John River near Westfield, NB: first lit 1 June 1882; present tower rebuilt in the 1930s after floods.

lens.note: Apparatus of the 1882 light, as the Department's report is quoted by LighthouseFriends. The present apparatus is not described in the sources read.

structures.note: 36 ft (11 m) high to the vane, standing on a small timber crib (LighthouseFriends quoting the 1882 report). Replaced in the 1930s.

structures.type: square pyramidal wood tower with lantern and gallery, painted white with red trim
structures.note: Present tower. Rebuilt and moved slightly after severe floods in the 1930s; the exact year is not given. Height 11.9 m per the CCG list; LighthouseFriends gives 11.3 m and Rowlett 11 m. LighthouseFriends describes a vinyl-clad tapered wood tower on pylons.

access.note: Reached by road, parking available; the entrance from Route 102 is unmarked (Rowlett). Grounds open, tower closed (Rowlett; LighthouseFriends).

events.note: Parliament appropriated $800 for a light at Belyeas Point (LighthouseFriends).
Tower contract of $395 awarded to Saunders Clark of Carleton. Square wooden tower, 36 ft high to the vane (LighthouseFriends).
Spafford Barker Belyea first keeper at an annual salary of $80 (LighthouseFriends).
Day, W. A. appointed 20 September 1899 at Belyea Point (keepers' table in the report printed 1906; matched by column position in the OCR).
Mrs. W. A. Day at the station from 1906 (LighthouseFriends). The 1908 table gives appointment 21 November 1906 (page image checked).

corrections.proposed: two towers: the first, a wooden square tower built 1882 (36 ft); the present one, rebuilt in the 1930s after floods, 11.9 m (CCG list)
corrections.why: The 1882 tower was replaced after 1930s floods. The 11.9 m height belongs to the present tower, and the 1882 date to the first one.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The CCG list gives 12.7 m. LighthouseFriends gives 13.6 m and Rowlett gives 14 m (45 ft). The record keeps the CCG list, which is the current official list. The difference is recorded, not resolved.
The CCG list gives a nominal range of 4 nautical miles. LighthouseFriends gives 5 miles. The CCG figure is kept.
The present tower is 11.9 m on the CCG list, 11.3 m on LighthouseFriends and 11 m on Rowlett. The record keeps 11.9 m.

Rowlett describes a square pyramidal wood tower with lantern and gallery. LighthouseFriends describes a vinyl-clad, four-sided, tapered wood tower on pylons. The sources disagree and both are recorded in the note.

notes_for_editor: Thin-to-moderate. Nearly all station detail comes from LighthouseFriends, a community site used for facts only. The Department's reports from 1882 and 1899 are not in the corpus (its Marine reports start in 1900), so the 1881 appropriation, the 1882 contract, the 1882 apparatus, the tower description (the 1882 report as LighthouseFriends quotes it) and Spafford Belyea's tenure rest on LighthouseFriends alone. Both keepers' tables were checked on the page images: 'Day, W. A', Belyea Point, Sept. 20, 1899, 90 00 (printed 1906, scan 341, printed p. 260; row aligned), and 'Day, Mrs. W. A', Belyea Point, Nov. 21, 1906, 90 00 (printed 1908, scan 149, printed p. 142; the year is on the image, not in the OCR). The corpus holds no Marine report after 1924, so the 1930s rebuild and the end year 1923 rest on LighthouseFriends and Rowlett. Wikipedia's lead names the light after Hendrick Belyea, a United Empire Loyalist settler. That is not verified here and is not used. A 1911 report's 'Belyea's' wharf light is at another place on the river, not this station. Rowlett's Sand Point entry is a neighbouring light, not this one. Brief errors: the standing tower is not the 1882 tower; the 1882 tower was wooden. The present CCG status is 'seasonal', which the brief's 'active' does not show. The keeper staffing status after 1923 is not in the sources read. Focal height and range disagree across sources (CCG 12.7 m and 4 NM; LighthouseFriends 13.6 m and 5 M; Rowlett focal plane 14 m); the story uses the CCG figures.
